{"body": "Nearly half of pytest's time goes to tests that check release rules through real `git` processes. Testing those rules at the planner, with plain data as input, would cut CI wall time noticeably. pytest is 77 % of the CI job (74–88 s of about 110 s).

## Evidence

- 286 test functions average 1 s or more per case. They are 9 % of the functions and take 626 s of the suite's 1,292 s summed test time (48 %)
- They sit in a few files:

  | File | Functions ≥ 1 s | What makes them slow |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test_worktrees` | 39 | real `git worktree` add, remove and prune per case |
  | `test_lanes` | 27 | release planning against a real repo with origin, tags and merges |
  | `test_pr_gate` | 27 | the `pr_gate.py` skill script in a subprocess, each with a git repo |
  | `test_fragments` | 20 | changelog fragments through real release commits |
  | `test_breaking_hold` | 18 | planner decisions through a real repo |
  | `test_gate_prune` | 15 | worktree pruning on real worktrees |
  | `test_milestone_status`, `test_milestones`, `test_publish_first`, `test_gate` | 39 | planner and status through real git |

- cProfile of `test_breaking_hold.py` plus `test_worktrees.py` (85 tests, 141 s serial): 123 s (86 %) is `subprocess.run`, about 24 calls per test, 1,660 of them through `shipmill.gitrepo.run`. Fixtures are not the cost: the `repo` fixture is already a template copied per worker
- Installs are not the cost either: `uv sync` is cached and under 3 s

## Proposal

The contracts stay: these tests assert the release rules that are the product (version, lane, hold, promotion). Change the level they test at:

- give the planner its inputs (tags, commits, changelog text, now) as data and assert each rule at that function, with no git
- keep a few end-to-end tests per lane that go through real git
- 109 of the 286 also carry other evidence of value (a unique branch, a CI catch, or a spec criterion's only test), so each moves rather than goes

This touches how the planner takes its inputs, so it starts as a spec.

## Not the cost

- Deleting every test that only overlaps others by coverage would save about 9 s of CI wall time (see the consolidation issue)
- Agent sessions: until #657 (2026-10-27) the gate's agents ran the full suite serially and tests took 51 % of the gate's active time. Since then it is 13 %, so that cost is already gone

Found by a test audit of `65f34d6e` (2026-10-30).
